The concept of "zero-shot generalization" in text-to-image models refers to the ability of a model to generate images that are not only similar to the training data but also novel and unseen. 

This phenomenon occurs when a model can produce images that are not only plausible but also coherent and meaningful, without requiring any additional training data. 

The model's ability to generalize to new and unseen concepts is a significant advancement in the field of text-to-image synthesis.
